original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-functor-equivalence}
Let $A$ and $B$ be rings. If
$$
F : \text{Mod}_A \longrightarrow \text{Mod}_B
$$
is an equivalence of categories, then there exists an isomorphism
$A \to B$ of rings and an invertible $B$-module $L$ such that
$F$ is isomorphic to the functor $M \mapsto (M \otimes_A B) \otimes_B L$.
hold_reason: Stacks Conventions (pinned conventions.tex, Algebra) define 'ring' as commutative with 1. Without that global assumption, the proposed standalone theorem is false: module categories over a field k and a matrix ring M_n(k) are equivalent by Morita theory although their rings are not isomorphic for n>1. The proposal needs the commutativity hypothesis made explicit.
proposed_correction: Say 'Let A and B be commutative rings with identity' before the equivalence assumption, preserving the invertible B-module and isomorphism conclusion; obtain a second independent source-first review.
